beats.narration_text: Hi — this is Bella, for Chaitanya. This video is about how the AI tutor actually knows the textbook — through lookup, not training. Almost everyone guesses wrong about this, and the guess changes how you judge the whole system.

show.event: cream Claude page; the serif greeting 'Ciao, HAI' sets above the composer with the terracotta spark — frame is already dressed at t=0, nothing empty
the ask types itself into the composer, character by character
send button arms terracotta; runningText 'tracing the answer…' begins
three result lines land in order — the ask comes back ANSWERED, so the reel opens on a receipt
HAI H-mark bug settles lower-right at low opacity

props.command: There is an AI tutor inside our textbooks. Faculty assume we trained a model on the book. Explain — for someone with no engineering background — what actually happens when a student asks it a question, and why that design was chosen.
output: nothing is trained — the model is rented, off the shelf
the book is searched first; the passages ride along with the question
that is why a content fix fixes the tutor, and why it costs cents

beats.narration_text: When people hear there's an AI tutor inside a textbook, they assume we fed the book to the AI and it learned it. That is not what happens. Nothing is trained on the textbook. There is no training run, and no model of our own anywhere in this project.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: the textbook and the model sit already drawn on the stage, with the arrow between them dashed and unresolved — the assumption is on screen before the voice names it

show.at: on 'fed the book to the AI'
show.event: the arrow solidifies and a 'trained on it' label snaps onto it — the guess completes itself
a single heavy terracotta X strikes through the arrow
the arrow and its label grey out and drop away, leaving the book and the model unconnected
a small mono line settles under the model: 'rented, not built'

beats.narration_text: The model we use is OpenAI's, off the shelf — the same one anybody can rent. It never changes. It doesn't know our books, and it never will. So how does it answer a question about chapter twelve? It looks it up.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: the rented model card is already on the stage, drawn and labelled, with its three facts as empty rules waiting to be filled
fact one writes: 'the same one anybody can rent'
fact two writes: 'it never changes'
fact three writes: 'it doesn't know our books'
the question 'what's in chapter twelve?' arrives at the card and stalls against it
the stalled question turns and a terracotta arrow redirects it away from the model, toward the book — the answer to the beat's own question, shown

facts: the same one anybody can rent
props.question: what's in chapter twelve?

beats.narration_text: Here's the real sequence. A student asks a question. Before that question reaches the model that writes the answer, the system searches the textbook and pulls out the handful of passages most relevant to what was asked.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: the question bubble and the open book are both already on the stage, the book's pages ruled with grey text lines
the question bubble lights and its text completes
a search sweep runs down the book's ruled lines
passage cards lift off the page one at a time, each highlighted

show.at: on 'most relevant to what was asked'
show.event: a trailing ellipsis settles after the lifted cards — the group reads as A HANDFUL, never as a stated count, because no source gives the number

beats.narration_text: Then it sends both things together: the question, and those passages. So the model isn't remembering the book. It's handed the relevant pages at the moment it's asked, and it answers from what's in front of it. It's an open-book exam, not a study session.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: the question and the passage stack are already side by side on the left, the model card already drawn on the right — the author's one-visual-carries-it frame, mid-mechanism
question and passages merge into a single envelope and travel as one to the model
a struck-through 'remembering' label falls away from the model card
the envelope opens INSIDE the model card — the passages are visibly in front of it, not inside it

show.at: on 'open-book exam, not a study session'
show.event: the phrase sets once in serif beneath the diagram, plain, no ornament, no second appearance anywhere in the reel

props.question: what's in chapter twelve?
props.landingPhrase: an open-book exam, not a study session

beats.narration_text: This sounds like a workaround. It's actually the better design, for three reasons. First: you can fix things. Correct a mistake in chapter twelve and the tutor is corrected too. If it had been trained, you would have to train it again.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: the chapter page is already open on the stage with a wrong line visible in it, and the tutor's answer card below already repeats that wrong line
the reason ledger opens at the top with slot one filled and two and three waiting
the wrong line is struck and the corrected line types in above it
the same correction propagates down into the tutor's answer card — one edit, both changed

show.at: on 'you would have to train it again'
show.event: a greyed alternative path appears alongside, labelled with the retraining cycle it avoids

props.sparkLine: Fix the book, fix the tutor.

beats.narration_text: Second: it can cite. Because the answer came from specific passages, the tutor can point at the section it got them from. A trained model can't. It just knows things, and you can't check where from.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: both columns are already framed and headed — LOOKS IT UP on the left, TRAINED on the right — each holding the same answer card
the reason ledger advances to slot two
a line draws from the left answer back to a named section, which lights terracotta
the right answer's line gropes toward its source and dead-ends in a dashed question mark
the two column verdicts resolve: CHECKABLE / NOT CHECKABLE

beats.protected: Author's instruction: this is the detail people repeat afterwards. Keep the numbers (a cent vs hundreds a month). Never trimmed, never dropped from the short.
beats.narration_text: Third: it's dramatically cheaper. Renting a model per question costs about a cent. Running our own would need a GPU server on all day — hundreds of dollars a month, before anyone asked a single question.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: both cost rows are already drawn and labelled — RENT and SELF-HOST — with their bars at zero and their figures blank
the reason ledger advances to slot three
the rent bar grows to a sliver and its figure counts up to about one cent, per question

show.at: on 'a GPU server on all day'
show.event: the self-host bar begins growing and does not stop at the frame's edge — it runs off the right of the stage
its figure settles at hundreds of dollars a month

show.at: on 'before anyone asked a single question'
show.event: a terracotta note lands under the long bar: 'at zero questions' — the bar is the idle cost, which is the whole point

beats.narration_text: There is one catch worth knowing. That search only works because the textbook was indexed ahead of time — catalogued, so it can be searched quickly. By default, that index is rebuilt whenever the book is built.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: the book and the empty index cabinet are both already drawn, the cabinet's slots ruled and unfilled
entries flow from the book's pages into the cabinet's slots and fill them
a search probe hits the filled cabinet and returns instantly
the trigger chip writes in, and the words BY DEFAULT sit in terracotta on it — the hedge is on screen, not just in the voice, because the trigger was not confirmable in code
the chip completes: 'rebuilt when the book is built'

props.triggerBody: rebuilt when the book is built

beats.narration_text: But if the content changes and the index doesn't get rebuilt, the tutor keeps answering from the old version. Confidently. With no error and no warning. So if a tutor ever seems to be describing a chapter that no longer exists — that's the first thing to check.

show.event: OPENING STATE IS NOT EMPTY: book and index sit side by side, already drawn and already IN STEP, both stamped with the same version — the healthy state is established before it breaks
the book's version advances; the index's version does not move
the index greys out and a drift gap opens visibly between the two version stamps
the tutor's answer card fills from the GREY index, not the current book
a confidence meter on the answer card runs to full while the answer itself is stale
two empty slots where an error and a warning would be stay conspicuously blank
the index — not the model, not the prompt — is ringed in terracotta

props.answerText: describing a chapter that no longer exists
